newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ireland's Ryanair says to start Sweden-UK flights.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's Ryanair says to start Sweden-UK flights.

text.p: Irish airline Ryanair said on Wednesday that it was starting daily flights between London's Stansted airport and Stockholm's Skavsta airport.
Airline spokesman John Donegan said Ryanair would run two return flights a day on the route starting from June 12.
The first will leave London at 0715 GMT and return from Stockholm at 1050 and the second will leave London at 1620 GMT and head back from Stockholm at 1955 arriving in London 2105.
"Ryanair, Europe's largest low fare airline, will reduce fares to Stockholm by over 50 percent," the company said in a statement.
Ryanair said over 70 percent of the seats would be available at the two lowest fares of 99 stg and 129 stg return.
The airline would also make available same/next day return fares to the business market for 199 stg return.
"Ryanair will break the duopoly of SAS and British Airways on the London-Stockholm route," Ryanair's chief executive Michael O'Leary said in a statement.

Ryanair said passengers could connect with London Stansted airport by the Skytrain from Liverpool Street station and the flying time to Stavsta was 15 minutes less than to Stockholm's major international airport Arlanda.
A bus service costing 10 stg return runs from Stavsta into Stockholm city centre.
Ryanair has been operating for 12 years and has a fleet of 17 Boeing 737-200 aircraft.
The airline said it expected to carry four million passengers in 1997 of whom 200,000 would fly on the new London-Stockholm route.
Ryanair currently flies to and from Ireland, England, and Scotland, and has connections from Dublin to Paris, Beauvais and Brussels.
